oneLiner: A slow-growth hybrid-cloud software and mainframe franchise that converts profit to cash and pays it out. After the July crash the market is betting that Q2 2026 was a timing miss, not the start of AI budgets crowding out IBM's software.

verdict.summary: Q3 2026 answered the July question in IBM's favour: growth came back to +5% and roughly two-thirds of the slipped mainframe and software deals closed. But the full-year guide was not raised, so Q4 decelerates again, and much of software's growth is still bought (Confluent, HashiCorp) with a balance sheet carrying ~$53B of net debt. The base case on FY2027 operating EPS at a high-teens multiple returns only mid-single digits plus the ~3% dividend; the bear case needs organic software to stall, the bull case needs it to visibly accelerate. A Q4 print with software organic growth near 5% and FCF above $15.7B would move us to Positive; another deal-slip quarter would move us to Cautious.
wtb: FY2026 revenue lands inside the unchanged 4-5% cc guide, which needs Q4 2026 revenue of roughly $20.0-20.7B against $19.7B in Q4 2025.
Software grows at least 7% in FY2027 with Confluent fully in the base from Q2 2027, i.e. organic software growth of mid-single digits rather than the flat organic rate disclosed for Q2 2026.
FY2026 free cash flow exceeds $15.7B (2025's $14.7B plus more than $1B), which needs Q4 FCF above ~$7.9B after $7.8B year to date.
The market keeps paying ~19x operating EPS at end-2027, which requires FY2027 operating EPS growth of ~8% and no new deal-slip warning.

bear.why: The Q2 2026 budget rotation proves structural: FY2027 revenue grows only ~2% on FY2026's ~$70.3B as organic software stalls, consulting stays flat and the z17 cycle fades. Operating net margin slips to ~16.3% as acquisition interest and integration costs bite. The market prices IBM as an ex-growth, levered dividend stock.

base.why: Revenue grows ~4% (the low end of the medium-term model): Red Hat and Data carry software to ~7%, consulting grows low single digits, infrastructure dips post-z17 but Distributed holds up. Productivity lifts operating net margin ~0.6pt to ~17.4%. A high-teens multiple holds because FCF keeps compounding and the dividend is covered.

bull.why: Revenue grows ~6.5%: slipped deals are fully recovered, Confluent and HashiCorp accelerate bookings, and gen AI turns consulting back to growth. Operating net margin reaches ~18%. The market re-rates IBM toward the low-20s it paid before the July warning as organic software growth is visibly mid-to-high single digit.

scenarioModel.note: EPS is IBM operating (non-GAAP) EPS, the basis IBM guides and the market values. EPS = FY2027 revenue x operating net margin / ~950M diluted shares (Q3 2026 weighted diluted 953.5M; buybacks roughly offset stock comp): bear $71.5B x 16.3% = $11.65B -> $12.27; base $73.2B x 17.4% = $12.74B -> $13.41; bull $75.0B x 18.0% = $13.50B -> $14.21. FY2026 revenue ~$70.3B assumes $50.2B YTD plus ~$20.1B in Q4. Multiples apply to FY2027 EPS at end-2027. The ~$1.69 quarterly dividend (~$6.76 a year) is not included in the page's return. Scenario inputs are Siberforge estimates, not consensus.

debates.q: Was Q2 2026 a timing miss or the start of AI crowd-out?
debates.bull: Q3 revenue growth recovered to +5% (+6% cc) from +1%, about two-thirds of the delayed mainframe and software deals closed, and transaction processing swung to +9% from -8% in Q2.
debates.bear: The 4-5% cc guide was only reaffirmed, not raised, after a beat, so Q4 growth slows back to roughly 2-5%; the quality check shows growth decelerating from +9-12% to +1% over four quarters, and one-third of the slipped deals is still out.
debates.view: Mostly timing, but not proven: the Q3 rebound includes recovered deals that flatter one quarter. The multiple stays high-teens only if Q4 holds growth at 4%+ without help from catch-up deals.

signpost.metric: Q4 2026 revenue growth (cc) and software growth
signpost.threshold: bullish if revenue +5% cc or better with software +8%+; bearish if revenue below +3% cc

debates.q: How much of software growth is organic?
debates.bull: Red Hat grew 11% with bookings accelerating to the high teens and OpenShift ARR at $2.4B; Data +19% and Confluent bookings ~+20% show the acquired assets are growing, not just being consolidated.
debates.bear: Q2 2026 organic software growth was flat by IBM's own disclosure; Confluent (closed Mar 17, 2026) is not in the Q3 2025 base, so a large part of the +8% is acquired. Automation fell 3% in Q3.
debates.view: This sets the multiple more than total growth does. We assume organic software of ~4-5% in the base case (Siberforge estimate; IBM did not disclose an organic rate in the Q3 release). Confluent laps in Q2 2027; reported software growth after that is the real test.

signpost.metric: Software organic growth (call disclosure) and Q2 2027 software growth once Confluent laps
signpost.threshold: organic 5%+ = re-rate case; organic below 2% = bear case
signpost.when: Q4 2026 call (late Jan 2027) and Q2 2027 report (Jul 2027)

debates.q: Can FCF carry the net debt and the dividend?
debates.bull: Q3 FCF was $3.0B (+$0.7B YoY), YTD $7.8B (+$0.6B), and the FY guide was raised to more than $1B of growth; capex is under 2% of revenue and cash conversion runs at 139% of net income (TTM).
debates.bear: Total debt was $63.8B at Sep 30, 2026 against $11.1B of cash: ~$53B net (about $40B excluding the $12.7B of IBM Financing debt). The dividend absorbs ~$6.4B a year and 2026 acquisition spend ran to ~$10.5B, so the cushion for more buying is thin.
debates.view: Manageable at IBM's investment-grade cash generation, which is why it is a risk and not a debate-breaker. It becomes one if FCF misses $15.7B while IBM keeps buying growth with debt.

signpost.metric: FY2026 free cash flow and year-end net debt
signpost.threshold: FCF above $15.7B and net debt flat-to-down = fine; FCF below $15.2B = cut base probability

thesis: Recurring software is the earnings engine. Software is ~45% of revenue and ~80% recurring; Red Hat accelerated to +11% with high-teens bookings growth, and Data grew 19% in Q3 2026 with Confluent folded in.

Cash is real and growing. FCF guidance was raised after Q3 to more than $1B of growth on 2025's $14.7B, and trailing operating cash flow runs 139% of net income - the dividend is funded by cash, not accounting.

The mainframe is a cash annuity, not a melting ice cube. z17 delivered more than $1B of incremental revenue over six quarters versus prior programs and 85% of mainframe clients are holding or growing capacity, so the post-z17 decline is a cycle trough.

The bar is modest. The reverse DCF needs ~6% a year FCF growth against ~4% revenue growth delivered over three years - the price assumes more of the same, so steady execution is enough to earn the dividend plus mid-single-digit EPS growth.

latestQuarter.label: Q3 2026 (ended Sep 30, 2026; reported Oct 21, 2026)
points: Revenue $17.1B, +5% (+6% cc) vs $16.33B a year earlier and ~$16.83B consensus.
Software $7.8B +8% (+9% cc): Red Hat/hybrid cloud +11%, Data +19%, Transaction Processing +9%, Automation -3%.
Consulting $5.3B flat (+2% cc); Infrastructure $3.7B +4%: IBM Z -20%, Distributed Infrastructure +31%, record Storage quarter.
Operating gross margin 58.5% (-20bp); operating pre-tax margin 19.3% (+70bp). Operating EPS $2.95 (+11%) vs ~$2.86 consensus; GAAP EPS $2.30.
FCF $3.0B (+$0.7B YoY); YTD FCF $7.8B (+$0.6B). Cash $11.1B and total debt $63.8B (incl. $12.7B financing debt) at Sep 30.

latestProse: Q3 2026 (ended Sep 30; reported Oct 21). Revenue $17.1B grew 5% (6% cc), about $0.3B above consensus, after +1% in Q2; operating EPS $2.95 (+11%) beat by ~$0.09 and operating pre-tax margin rose 70bp to 19.3% even as operating gross margin slipped 20bp to 58.5%. Software ($7.8B, +8%) did the work: Red Hat +11%, Data +19% with Confluent in the numbers, and Transaction Processing back to +9% as roughly two-thirds of the mainframe and related software deals delayed from Q2 closed. Consulting was flat at $5.3B; Infrastructure rose 4% with IBM Z -20% against Distributed +31%. Free cash flow was $3.0B (+$0.7B). The disclosure that matters most: IBM beat by about $0.3B of revenue and still did not raise the revenue guide.
guidanceProse: FY2026: constant-currency revenue growth of 4-5% reaffirmed (the range was cut from 'more than 5%' on Jul 22), with currency neutral to growth at current rates. Free cash flow guidance raised to growth of more than $1B, from about $1B in July - i.e. above ~$15.7B on 2025's $14.7B. With $50.2B of revenue year to date, the unchanged range implies Q4 revenue of roughly $20.0-20.7B, +2-5% on Q4 2025's $19.7B (Siberforge arithmetic, FX-sensitive). Quarterly dividend held at $1.69 (record Nov 10, payable Dec 10, 2026). IBM does not give EPS guidance.

guide.label: FY26 guide (reaffirmed Oct 21, 2026)
guide.sub: FCF raised from +~$1B; revenue range unchanged after Q3 beat

segments: Software: $7.8B in Q3 2026, ~46% of revenue - Red Hat/hybrid cloud (OpenShift ARR $2.4B), automation (incl. HashiCorp, Apptio), data (incl. Confluent, watsonx), transaction processing; ~80% recurring.
Consulting: $5.3B, ~31% - strategy, technology and intelligent operations; AI ~30% of Q3 consulting revenue and ~35% of backlog (per Constellation Research coverage).
Infrastructure: $3.7B, ~22% - IBM Z (z17 cycle, now lapping), Power and Storage (Distributed +31% in Q3 2026).
Financing: $0.2B, ~1% - captive financing; carries $12.7B of the group's $63.8B debt.
competitive: MSFT, ORCL and the hyperscalers sit on the winning side of the AI budget rotation that hurt IBM in Q2 2026; IBM's answer is to be the hybrid and data layer (Red Hat, Confluent, HashiCorp) underneath them.
ACN read-across: discretionary consulting is soft industry-wide; IBM Consulting was flat in Q3 2026 at constant-currency +2%, in line with the peer group rather than share-gaining.
HPE and Dell compete for the server and storage spend that clients pulled forward in mid-2026; IBM Distributed Infrastructure (+31% in Q3) captured part of it.
Red Hat vs Broadcom/VMware: virtualization displacement keeps feeding OpenShift, whose ARR rose to $2.4B with accelerating growth.
Quantum: IBM signed 16 enterprise quantum engagements in 2026 to date and targets fault tolerance (Starling) in 2029; Google, Quantinuum and IonQ are the main rivals.
moat: Incumbency and switching costs: IBM Z runs core transaction systems at most large banks and insurers, and 85% of mainframe clients are maintaining or growing capacity. About 80% of software revenue is recurring, anchored by Red Hat's open-source position. The moat monetizes slow, durable growth and cash, not hypergrowth.
risks: Growth is lumpy and decelerating. The quality check shows four quarters going +9% -> +12% -> +9% -> +1% before Q3's +5%, and the unchanged guide implies Q4 slows again; another deal-slip quarter would make the July warning look structural (debate 1).

Software growth is partly bought. Organic software was flat in Q2 2026 and Confluent ($11.6B, closed Mar 2026) flatters reported growth until Q2 2027; goodwill was $74.6B at mid-2026 (prior note), so a stumble in integration shows up as an impairment as well as slower growth (debate 2).

Net debt is the balance-sheet risk. ~$53B of net debt at Sep 30, 2026 (down from $57.1B at Jun 30 on Q3 cash build) plus a ~$6.4B dividend leaves little room for another large acquisition without more borrowing (debate 3).
Consulting is stuck. Revenue has been flat for two years and gen AI deflates services pricing even as it fills the backlog.

Quantum spend is a cost before it is a revenue line. More than $10B committed over five years (prior note) against a 2029 fault-tolerance target; a slip removes narrative support while the spend stays in FCF.
catalysts: Nov 10 / Dec 10, 2026: dividend record and payment dates ($1.69); watch for any change in capital-allocation language (debate 3).
Dec 10, 2026: IBM Quantum Day - commercial engagements and roadmap milestones.
~Late Jan 2027: Q4 2026 report and 2027 guide - revenue growth, software organic rate, FY2026 FCF vs $15.7B (debates 1, 2, 3).
~Late Apr 2027: Q1 2027 report - first quarter of the new 2027 framework; last quarter before Confluent laps (debate 2).

valPresets.note: IBM is a steady FCF generator (guided above ~$15.7B for 2026 off $14.7B in 2025); presets bracket the ~6% a year growth the reverse DCF says is priced in.
